claims.text: Cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr has 8–16% room-temperature tensile ductility.
Cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr has a yield strength of 163–530 MPa at 1000 °C.
Untreated cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr has poor high-temperature oxygen resistance.
A 2–5 μm high-purity Al2O3 PVD coating with an intermediate bonding layer and post-deposition anneal will form a continuous, adherent barrier on cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr.
Post-deposition annealing at 1000 °C for 1–2 hours in an inert atmosphere will relieve coating stress.
Post-deposition annealing at 1000 °C for 1–2 hours in an inert atmosphere will promote coating adherence.
The coating and bonding interlayer will produce a continuous, dense alumina surface layer.
The continuous, dense alumina layer will act as a diffusion barrier to oxygen.
Alumina provides a thermodynamically stable, slow-growing oxide barrier under the proposed high-temperature conditions.
The alumina barrier will limit oxygen diffusion into the HfNbTaTiZr substrate.
The intermediate bonding layer will reduce thermal-expansion mismatch and mechanical stresses during high-temperature exposure.
Reducing interfacial mismatch and stress will prevent coating spallation or delamination.
The coating system will significantly improve oxidation resistance during exposure in air at 1000 °C for up to 100 hours.
The coating treatment will preserve 8–16% room-temperature tensile ductility.
The coating treatment will preserve yield strength within 163–530 MPa at 1000 °C under strain rates of 10^-4–10^-2 s^-1.
The surface treatment will not alter the bulk alloy composition.
